findings.finding: Publisher calls the suite medium/difficult and lists Prelude, Minuet, Adagio, Humoresque. Its local sample alt-preview.png shows only the opening Prelude: slow sustained upper-register lines, chromatic motion, overlapping entries and dynamic shaping. First two staves use solo tuning, lower two orchestral tuning. The other three movements were not inspected.

grade.basis: Informed whole-suite estimate: advanced upper-part register and controlled chromatic legato in the inspected opening suggest level 5 bass technique; exposed upper-voice tuning, blend and coordinated independence across four basses justify one ensemble level, yielding 6. Publisher whole-work difficulty description supports this band. No assertion of particular figures or register in unseen movements; pace and character describe the contrasting suite collectively.

findings.finding: The publisher technical description, retrieved in search indexing after direct access timed out/encountered a challenge, explicitly describes a four-movement work with an advanced top part and approximately 13-minute duration. No score notation was inspected.

IMSLP lists a 19-page manuscript in sounding pitch and specifies solo tuning for all four instruments. A complete manuscript link exists, but a notation preview was not obtained during this bounded review.

grade.basis: Whole-work placement at Advanced, level 5, follows the publisher explicit assessment of the top part. This is an independent translation onto the supplied bass exam-equivalent scale, not an official exam grade. No additional ensemble uplift is imposed without inspected notation or listening evidence. Exact register, bowing, rhythmic demands, tonal mode and movement-level technical extremes remain unverified. Moderate is a cautious aggregate pace placeholder for an uninspected four-movement work.

findings.finding: Publisher-associated description identifies a minimalist study in harmonics, a limited number of pitches for each player, high harmonics over Bass 12 pizzicato, and suitability for mixed abilities. The inspected local opening sample arietta-preview.jpg shows Allegretto at approximately quarter=120 in 3/4, simple sustained/repeated upper paired lines and staggered entries. It does not show later development or an active Bass 12 part.

grade.basis: Whole-work estimate uses the inspected opening plus the publisher description of the entire texture. Limited-pitch, rhythmically simple harmonic playing supports approximately level 3 for the most demanding upper voices, rather than treating treble clef alone as advanced stopped-note technique. Maintaining reliable soft harmonic response, balance and staggered layering across twelve independent players adds one ensemble level, yielding 4. Balanced identifies distributed upper-voice responsibility, not equal difficulty for all twelve parts. Only the opening page was inspected; no claim is made about unseen exact pitches or later techniques.
